root_cause.text: The function `dev_fwd_path()` in `net/core/dev.c` used a `WARN_ON_ONCE` to detect when the forward path stack exceeded `NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX`, but this condition can be deliberately triggered by userspace constructing a long chain of virtual net devices (e.g., IPIP tunnels), causing a kernel warning that can lead to a denial-of-service.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `WARN_ON_ONCE` check (line `if (WARN_ON_ONCE(k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX))` becomes `if (k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX)`), and the commit message states: “recent support for IPIP tunnels increases chances of reaching this WARN_ON_ONCE if userspace manages to build a sufficiently long forward path. Remove it.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary WARN_ON_ONCE from dev_fwd_path when the path stack is full to suppress expected runtime warnings.
intent_record.what: Replaced WARN_ON_ONCE(k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX) with a plain conditional check (if (k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX)) in dev_fwd_path.
intent_record.how: Previously, when the stack path count exceeded the maximum, a kernel warning was emitted once and NULL was returned. Now, only NULL is returned without any warning.
